transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-08-19 15:00 PT
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Product), Evan (LatentBridge Head of Search), Priya (LatentBridge Data Eng), Carlos (LatentBridge CTO)

Auto-generated summary: quick demo covering embeddings + reranking endpoints. Pilot discussed.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. we're pretty excited to show a quick rerank flow with the hosted embeddings and the reranker endpoint. can everyone see the screen?
00:08 Evan: yep, looks good. thanks Maya. quick context — we run a product search across 1.2M SKUs, mostly ecomm catalog, some long descriptions. current stack is in-house vectors on elastic + an expensive transformer-based reranker that is slow at scale.
00:22 Maya: great, that aligns with what you sent in the questionnaire. Liam will walk through the API and Console, i'll jump in on pricing and pilots.
00:30 Liam: cool, i'll start with a high level — Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint, you POST docs get vectors, we have pre-built models tuned for ecommerce embeddings; there's also a reranker endpoint that accepts candidate ids + embeddings and returns ranked list with scores and explainability tokens.
00:46 Priya: are those explainability tokens like SHAP? or do you mean token-level attention output?
00:52 Liam: it's lighter — we give top features and delta scores, not full SHAP. it's more like per-candidate signals and the text span matches. sometimes our auto-summaries are noisy — apologies if names get mangled, the transcriber picks up "redwood mass" sometimes.
01:12 Carlos: curious about latency — our SLO is 150ms p95 for the reranker, is that realistic on hosted?
01:19 Liam: short answer: depends on candidate size and model. for a 10-candidate rerank using the tuned small reranker model we typically see 60-110ms p95 in hosted for the configs we've benchmarked. for larger candidates or heavy context it can go up. we can show you the console latency breakdown.
01:40 Maya: and there are knobs — batching, quantized models, and prefix caching which Reduce token generation cost and can help latency in many flows.
01:50 Evan: can you show the Console? we want to see the request/response timings and token costs.
01:56 Liam: sure — pulling up the Redwood Console. here you can see a per-route dashboard, token breakdown, and an example rerank trace. notice the KV cache hit rate at the top right — that was from demo traffic.
02:18 Liam: we also surfaced a suggestion in Optimize: for this traffic profile we recommend the 8-bit quantized variant with continuous batching window of 50ms and a max batch size of 12; that gives good cost/latency balance.
02:36 Priya: what's the difference between hosted and dedicated here? like if we want single-tenant GPUs later.
02:42 Maya: Hosted is quickest to onboard — API keys, no infra for you to manage. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and stricter isolation, predictable throughput, and SLA. we often start customers on hosted for pilot, then move to dedicated if they need committed throughput or stricter data isolation.
03:01 Evan: data retention — for hosted, do you retain embeddings or customer text? we need to ensure PCI/PHI is not stored.
:03:08 Sofia: good question — by default hosted logs minimal request metadata and short-lived KV cache for performance, but customers can opt out of data retention and we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. for regulated data we recommend Private deployment.
03:28 Carlos: what's your compliance posture — SOC 2? any healthcare regs?
03:32 Maya: we are SOC 2 Type II certified, and we have HIPAA controls in place for Dedicated/Private setups. we'll share the security pack after the call.
03:42 Priya: ok thanks. can you show an example rerank request/response?
03:47 Liam: yes — loading the API request. example payload: query, topKCandidates (with embedding vectors), context. we send back scores and reranked ids. i'll run the small demo using the ecommerce test dataset.
04:12 [laptop typing sounds]
04:20 Liam: running now, sending a sample query "waterproof hiking jacket women's" to the embeddings + reranker flow. initial retrieval from vector store gives 50 candidates — we pass 12 into the reranker.
04:35 Transcript note: transcription sometimes splits words; apologies, "reranker" shows up as "re-ranker" in text.
04:42 Liam: results — top 5 with scores: 0.94, 0.87, 0.82, 0.77, 0.63. you can see the explainability anchors where the reranker scored the top item for 'waterproof' and 'breathable'.
05:05 Evan: looks promising. what about throughput? if we hit 2k qps of retrieval and 200 qps of rerank, how does that map to cost?
05:18 Maya: roughly: embeddings cost per document vector call, reranker cost per candidate matrix op. i'll share a cost model doc — for your projected traffic (2k retrieval -> 200 rerank) we estimate X per token monthly. we should run your dataset to get a real number.
05:36 Priya: do you support incremental indexing? we have frequent updates and need low-latency freshness.
05:42 Liam: yes, embeddings endpoint supports document upserts; we also have strategies for warm-up and prefix caching to avoid cold KV misses. if you have heavy update rate, we can tune the cache TTLs.
06:00 Evan: security again — SSO must be SAML with SCIM provisioning. can Redwood integrate?
06:06 Maya: yes, SSO and SCIM are supported for org accounts. for API-only access we can issue scoped API keys and rotate them.
06:15 Carlos: one more thing — any concerns about hallucination in reranker? sometimes rerankers boost irrelevant results due to model hallucinations.
06:23 Liam: great question — reranker is trained to prefer lexical and semantic alignment; we add penalty signals for long-distance hallucinated matches and we validate against labeled sets. plus Optimize can monitor quality regressions and alert if a new model variant causes drop in precision@k.
06:44 Priya: can we control model versioning via the Console?
06:48 Liam: yes — per-route model pinning and rollout controls. you can do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a prior model if error rates spike.
07:00 Evan: okay, very useful. what do you need from us to run a pilot?
07:04 Maya: sample queries and labels ideally 500-1k rows; define success metrics (precision@10, latency p95), timeline, and whether you want hosted or dedicated pilot. we usually do a 4-week pilot.
07:20 Carlos: we'd like hosted pilot first to validate relevance and cost, then evaluate Dedicated. timeline target: pilot start end of August.
07:28 Maya: sounds good. we'll provision sandbox, provide test keys, and run an initial baseline.
07:33 [brief cross talking]
07:40 Liam: i'll attach a small benchmark harness on GitHub — includes scripts to compute precision@k, latency traces, and cost estimator.
07:50 Priya: oh can you also include how to compute per-route token counts? ours engineering wants a reproducible script.
07:56 Liam: yes included.
08:01 Maya: just to recap — next steps: redwood sends SOW + pricing, SE shares benchmark repo and sample reranker script, LatentBridge shares 500 queries and labels, schedule pilot kickoff.
08:15 Evan: yep, and we'll internally confirm the compliance checklist and get back with SSO details.
08:22 Carlos: one question — if we find the hosted SLA insufficient, what's the path and lead time to Dedicated?
08:28 Maya: typically 4-6 weeks to provision Dedicated depending on region and GPU pool size; we'll include those timelines in the SOW.
08:37 Sofia: small note — Optimize UI also gives quantization trade-off charts so you can see cost vs quality delta before applying. it's a recommendation engine but you can also run A/B in Console.
08:50 Priya: perfect. any blockers we see now?
08:54 Evan: none from my side. maybe pricing — we'll wait for the sheet.
09:00 Maya: great thanks all. we'll follow up by end of week.

[call ends with quick social sign-off]

Recap (auto): Demo of hosted embeddings + reranker flow, Console observability, Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization, discussed security (SOC2, KMS, SSO), agreed to pilot and set action items.
notes: Transcript includes rough timestamps every few minutes; some speaker names are simplified. References: pilot SOW template (link), security pack (link), benchmark repo (github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-bench).
